# v0.29.2 — compaction gets past the scan limit and keeps exit headroom, and shutdown waits for it

v0.29.2 is a patch release on v0.29.1 and the first release train: it carries every fix that was ready when the train was cut. It fixes two compaction problems, one that could keep compaction from forming a summary on long tool-heavy sessions and one that could push the next request over the model's window. It also makes shutdown wait for a running compaction, stores a repeated tool call on hosts that reuse tool-call IDs, opens a profile's storage only when that profile is used, and lets the host open the bundled skill.

It adds one setting, `LCM_SHUTDOWN_COMPACTION_WAIT_S`, and the schema version stays 5. The release gate passed. Some rows are not green, each by a disclosed decision under **Release-manager decisions** (see **Qualification**): the reference-agent window, D2 and D3 (all not run), D8 on LongMemEval-S, and some bars of Phase C, of D5-B and of two host cells. The same list also records decisions on rows that passed: D1's batch-shape pre-check (which failed), the hand-run final steps of D1 LOCAL and D4, and the #1501 fault cells settled from repeats.

## Changes since v0.29.1

### Compaction

- **A contiguity stop at the scan limit no longer repeats on every pass.** A claim on a chunk row stored above a later chunk row held back every row behind it. When the walk stopped first, at the leaf budget or at the scan limit, the leaf came out empty with the contiguity reason, and the next pass picked the same chunk, so some long tool-heavy sessions never formed a summary. v0.29.1's larger-budget retry cleared the budget case. Compaction now also retries once on the part of the chunk before the blocking row, ending on a tool-group boundary. The rows after that point stay in the host's context, and the existing escape summarises them from the store with tool pairs kept whole. A retry that would take a claim from a row it cut is refused, and the leaf stays as it was. The stop is logged once per conversation (`LCM contiguity hole:`, with IDs, roles and counts only) ([#1998](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1998), [PR #2032](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2032)).
- **An exit fit keeps its headroom when the list is over the window.** An automatic compaction exit fits the list under 95% of the host's threshold, so the next turn has room. When the list was also over the model's window budget, the fit dropped that cap and stopped at the window budget. On a 262,144-token model, the next request then landed above the host's threshold, every later turn started over it, and the provider finally rejected a request as over the window. The fit now first cuts whole oldest turns down to the exit budget, keeping the summary prefix and every recent row. When no whole-turn cut is deep enough, it behaves as before, and the next request can then still land above the host's threshold. Only the live list is shorter; stored rows are untouched ([#2039](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2039), [PR #2050](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2050)).

### Shutdown

- **Shutdown waits for a running compaction.** A host's `shutdown()` on another thread could close the databases under a running compaction, which could lose that pass or crash the worker. Shutdown now marks the engine as closing, waits up to `LCM_SHUTDOWN_COMPACTION_WAIT_S` (default 10 s) for running passes to finish, and on a timeout logs one warning and leaves the connections open, so a later shutdown can close them. A running pass that sees the shutdown stops before its next write and returns the host's messages; writes it already committed stay committed. A pass that starts after shutdown began returns the host's messages unchanged and writes nothing ([#2101](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2101), [PR #2104](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2104)).

### Restarts and storage

- **A repeated tool call is stored when the host still shows the earlier one.** At the first turn after a restart, LCM-X proved a tool pair a replay by counting identical stored copies, including copies that the host's own history still shows before the point where matching resumes. On a host that reuses tool-call IDs, a new call and result that repeated an earlier pair exactly were then not stored. The copies the host's history accounts for are now set aside first, and a row recorded as a new occurrence is never skipped. When the earlier pair was compacted out of the host's view, the new pair can still be skipped (see **Known issues**). On such a host this change also has a known gap: after a restart whose stored copy of the earlier pair is older than the recent stored window, a tool step can be stored twice, or an old step stored in place of a new one (see **Known issues**, [#2197](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2197)) ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172), [PR #2185](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2185)).
- **A profile's storage opens on first real use.** Loading the plugin opened this profile's store right away, so another profile's gateway on the same host, which only loads the plugin, opened and held this profile's store and files. The store, its databases and the plugin's files now open on first real use, and a process that never uses a profile creates nothing for it. For the process's own home (the one `HERMES_HOME` names, or the default `.hermes` folder in the user's home when it is unset), the inactive-profile record is still written at load; `lcm_status` and `lcm_doctor` report it before storage opens ([#2152](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2152), [PR #2178](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2178)).

### Skill

- **The bundled skill opens with `skill_view`.** The plugin registered its skill folder instead of the skill file, so the host's `skill_view` tool failed on every operating system. It now registers `SKILL.md`. Capture, recall and compaction were not affected ([#571](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/571), [#2131](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2131), [PR #729](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/729)).

### Testing improved

- **New regression tests:** the contiguity-stop shapes and the prefix retry; the exit-fit headroom; shutdown during a compaction (a blocked pass, a timeout, passes that start while closing, and ingest that keeps running); a reused tool-call ID at a restart, with the compacted case pinned as a strict expected failure; 28 lazy-storage cells; and the registered skill path.
- **CI on release branches:** CI now runs on pushes and pull requests to `release/v*.x` maintenance branches, so each release-train head is checked without a manual run ([#2171](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2171), [PR #2190](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2190)).

## On by default in this release

Every change above is on by default. The one new setting, `LCM_SHUTDOWN_COMPACTION_WAIT_S`, sets how long shutdown waits for a running compaction. Local semantic recall stays on by default, as in v0.29.0.

## Upgrade

- **Host:** Hermes 0.21.3 or newer is still required (0.21.5 or newer recommended), with Python 3.11 or newer.
- **Store:** the schema version stays 5, with no new tables, columns or triggers.
- **Settings:** one added. `LCM_SHUTDOWN_COMPACTION_WAIT_S` (seconds, default `10.0`, environment only) bounds how long shutdown waits for a running compaction. Invalid, negative and non-finite values use `10.0`, and values above `86400` are capped there.
- **From v0.29.0 or older:** follow the v0.29.1 upgrade notes first, including its note on the first restart after the upgrade.
- **Rollback:** target `v0.29.1`, which ignores the new setting. Take a SQLite-safe backup first (see `docs/operator-guide.md`), and compare ordered raw messages and summary provenance through upgrade, rollback and re-upgrade.

## Known issues

- **Some compaction passes still write no summary** ([#1880](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1880)): a pass that forms no summary input (a tool group the host keeps half of, a contiguity stop, or rows with no stored source) writes no summary but still returns a rebuilt copy of the host's list, which the host commits. Returning the host's original list on such passes is planned for a v0.30.x release after v0.30.0, because the fix tried for this release did not pass review. It matters because, on the reference agent, one such pass made the host rewrite its history and rebuild its prompt cache. The contiguity stop that repeated on every pass of some long tool-heavy sessions is cleared for both known causes (see **Compaction** above); an ignored row just before the cut tool group, or a retry refused because it would take a cut row's claim, can still keep that shape stuck, no worse than v0.29.1; the ignored-row case's fix is part of the [#1993](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1993) design. Nothing is lost. On a group whose request stays above the preflight limit and whose only progress is on hidden rows, the escape can spend about 80 to 130 s on a pass the host cannot use before a cold turn's first reply (first output came at about 95 to 162 s on the reference agent, on first turns after restarts). Moving this work out of the wait before a reply is tracked for the compaction-you-don't-notice release ([#2173](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2173)).
- **Survival-fit rotations leave no compaction record:** when a session rotates because the survival fit trimmed the live view, the new session gets no record of what the previous one compacted, so rows stored under earlier sessions may not be matched to their stored copies. A compaction that is already blocked on such rows can then stay blocked, and while it is blocked each survival fit trims older rows from what the model sees with no summary in their place. Its frequency on its own is unknown. No stored rows are lost: the store keeps every row and recall can still reach them. A fix is tracked for a v0.30.x release after v0.30.0 ([#2029](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2029)).
- **A rare message loss after two compactions in a row is under investigation** ([#2330](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2330)): in one run of the reliability test matrix, two messages that arrived right after a compaction rotated the session were never stored, because a second compaction ran in the new session before the turn ended. It has not been reproduced: the failing cell was repeated 8 times on the same host with full logging, and all 8 passed. The session-end path it involves is unchanged from v0.29.1, and this release's reliability matrix showed no new failure against v0.29.1, but no run measured whether this release's compaction fixes make the trigger, a second compaction right after a rotation, more frequent. If it recurs, that run's stores and logs are kept for the fix, which ships in a later release.
- **Slow summaries can shrink the live view:** when summary calls time out at the compaction threshold, the survival fit can drop about 80–115 older rows from what the model sees. The store keeps every row and recall can still reach them; a fix is tracked for the compaction-you-don't-notice release ([#2004](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2004)).
- **A slow, rejected summary can hold compaction for 600 s** ([#2272](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2272)): when a summary call is slow and its result is rejected, the pass can stop as if it ran out of time, which holds compaction for 600 s. While the hold lasts, the oldest live turns leave the model's context, including some that no summary covers, and lifting the hold does not bring them back. By a reading of the code, they stay stored and recall can still reach them. It was seen in 2 of 54 benchmark replays (see the D2 and D3 decision below). A fix is planned for a v0.30.x release after v0.30.0.
- **The exit fit's headroom cut can drop rows no summary covers** ([#2184](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2184)): when an automatic exit fit is over the window budget, the cut this release adds takes whole old turns out of the model's view down to the exit budget, and it can take rows no summary covers. On the reported shape that is about 36,000 tokens more than the window alone needs. The store keeps every row and recall can still reach them. A fix is not scheduled yet; it is tracked in the backlog.
- **Reasoning text is not counted or stored** ([#2233](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2233)): on reasoning models whose host sends earlier reasoning back to the model, LCM-X's token count leaves that reasoning out, so compaction can start later than it should, and a request can be larger than the exit fit's headroom allows for. The store keeps the messages and replies but not that reasoning text. A fix is tracked for the compaction-you-don't-notice release.
- **Catalog install on upstream Hermes with the plugin scanner:** the upstream catalog entry pins v0.29.1's payload ([Hermes #148452](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/148452), merged 2026-11-05), and an update to this release's payload follows its GA. Until then, a catalog install gets an older release. So does a fresh Hermes 0.23.0 client while the live catalog is larger than the client's 2 MiB size cap ([Hermes #151856](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/151856)): such a client falls back to the catalog copy shipped with 0.23.0, which pins v0.29.1. For this release, use `scripts/install.sh`, or pin its commit as the README's update section shows (`--ref` with the v0.29.2 tag's 40-character commit SHA). Hermes v0.22.6 and newer rate v0.29.1's payload `safe`: their scanner counts the small-host CPU detector's read-only `/proc/self` reads as low severity ([Hermes #146352](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/146352)), and this release does not change that detector. Hermes v0.22.5 and older rate it `caution` (not `safe`) for those reads; nothing was changed to hide them from the scanner ([#1946](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1946)). Hermes 0.21.3's scanner blocks a `caution` verdict from a community source, so a catalog install there needs `--force` after reviewing the findings, or `scripts/install.sh`.
- **Upstream Hermes manual `/compress`:** on Hermes stable releases up to v0.22.5, a manual `/compress` from the gateway uses the host's own compressor and bypasses LCM-X, so stored history can gain duplicate replies. No rows were lost in the reported cases. Upstream Hermes fixed this on 2026-10-28 and shipped the fix in Hermes v0.22.6 and newer ([Hermes #145806](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/145806), fixing [#143587](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/143587)): `/compress` now runs the session's LCM-X engine. The LCM-X defence, planned for a v0.30.x release after v0.30.0, stays until the oldest supported Hermes includes the fix ([#1922](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1922), [#1924](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1924)).
- **Shutdown during a compaction, two edge cases** ([#2183](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2183)): if shutdown stops an overflow-recovery pass, the pass returns the host's list without fitting it and does not record that recovery failed; and if a pass had already committed leaves when shutdown stopped it, its status still reads `noop` ("engine shutting down"). Both need a shutdown to start during a pass. Stored rows are not affected.
- **Shutdown does not wait for an ingest outside a compaction** ([#2193](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2193)): an ingest started by the preflight check or by an `lcm_*` tool call is not counted as a running compaction, so a shutdown at that moment can close the store under it. That ingest then fails and rolls back, so nothing is written half-way and the host still holds the messages. It needs a shutdown at the same moment as such an ingest.
- **A gateway stop can leave a session's last messages unstored** ([#2253](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2253)): if the store is busy when a session ends, LCM-X keeps that session's last messages in memory and retries later. When the Hermes gateway stops, it exits without giving LCM-X its final retry, so those messages are missing from the store until the session is resumed; after `/new` they are not recovered. It needs a busy store at the last session end before the stop. That session end logs a warning that a retry is pending, but nothing is logged when the stop skips the retry. The host still holds the messages. A fix is planned for v0.30.0.
- **The inactive-profile record on another home layout** ([#2152](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2152)): when `HERMES_HOME` is unset and Hermes uses a platform default home other than the `.hermes` folder in the user's home, LCM-X treats the process's own home as another profile's. Its inactive-profile record is then kept in memory and written only at first real use, so a process that never uses storage does not save it; `lcm_status` and `lcm_doctor` in that process still report it. Stored messages are not affected.
- **Retry shapes still being fixed** (all are redesigned together for a v0.30.x release after v0.30.0, including the cases that can lose a row, #1837, #1838 and one window of #1451):
  - after a tool call is retried with new message IDs, each later cold restart can store that call and its result again: one more copy per restart, nothing lost ([#1836](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1836));
  - after a cold restart, if only the tool result's message ID changes on a retry, the new result may not be stored ([#1837](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1837));
  - if the plugin restarts before a session's first compaction and the host re-sends the last tool turn with a new timestamp on its user message, that user message and its tool pair may not be stored ([#1838](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1838));
  - in some retry and restart sequences after compaction, a replaced or retried message can be dropped or stored twice ([#1451](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1451)).
  Real-host frequency is unknown.
- **Crash before a reply, then rotation:** on hosts that do not give messages unique IDs, if the agent crashes before replying and the conversation then rotates, the next turn can be stored twice. A fix is planned for a v0.30.x release after v0.30.0 ([#1508](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1508)).
- **Duplicates kept on purpose:** turns stored before v0.29.0's carried-stamp marker can be stored again by a replay, and user messages that the host itself mirrors after an ACP crash recovery are kept twice. LCM-X keeps both copies rather than risk losing a genuine message; see `docs/identity-ledger.md` ([#1501](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1501), [PR #1775](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1775)).
- **Restarts can store old rows again:** at a long conversation's first turn after a gateway restart, the host rebuilds the conversation and hands its assistant and tool rows to LCM-X without their timestamps, and LCM-X can store rows it already holds a second time, as on v0.28.x, v0.29.0 and v0.29.1. Nothing is lost, but recall can show a row several times, one more copy per restart. A fix is planned for a v0.30.x release after v0.30.0, because it builds on the ingest record that v0.30.0 adds ([#1674](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1674)).
- **A restart can store a tool result again without its call:** at a session's first turn after a restart (a cold bind), if the point where LCM-X resumes matching falls between a tool call and its result, the result can be stored a second time without the call. Nothing is lost, and the copy is not sent to the model as a stored row (a result without its call is dropped from the model's context), but recall can show it twice. v0.29.0 and v0.29.1 behave the same. A fix is planned for v0.30.0 ([#2163](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2163)), because it needs the ingest record that v0.30.0 adds.
- **A restart can skip a repeated tool call after its earlier copy was compacted out** ([#2172](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2172)): at a session's first turn after a restart, on a host that reuses tool-call IDs (for example `call_0` on every turn), a new tool call and result that exactly repeat a pair already compacted out of the host's view can be taken for a replay and not stored. The host keeps them, but LCM-X's store does not, so recall cannot find them. Hosts that give each tool call a unique ID are not affected. Hermes keeps the ID a model provider sends and renames one that repeats, so its IDs are unique whenever the provider sends them, as the reference agent's provider does; with a provider that sends no ID, Hermes derives the ID from the call's name, arguments and position in its turn, so an identical call made again gets the same ID. This release fixes the case where the host still shows the earlier pair; the compacted case needs the ingest record that v0.30.0 adds, and its fix is planned for a v0.30.x release after v0.30.0.
- **A forced restart point can store a tool step twice on hosts that reuse tool-call IDs** ([#2197](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2197)): on a host that reuses tool-call IDs, if the point where matching resumes after a restart lands after a stored copy of an earlier tool step that is older than the recent stored window, this release can store a tool step twice, or store an old step in place of a new one, where v0.29.1 stores it correctly. It was reached only with an injected restart point; no normal path without a fault has been found to reach it, and one narrow path, which needs native recovery turned on under v0.23.3 to v0.24.9, is not resolved. Hosts that give each tool call a unique ID are not affected; on Hermes, that holds whenever the model provider sends tool-call IDs, as the reference agent's does (see the item above). A fix is planned for a v0.30.x release after v0.30.0.
- **A re-made identical tool step can be skipped after a cold start** ([#2259](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2259)): at a session's first turn after a restart, a new tool call and result that are byte-identical to rows already stored (same tool-call ID, same result, same following user text) can be taken for a replay and not stored, even when the host's timestamp or message ID shows they are new. On Hermes this needs a model provider that sends no tool-call IDs, so that the repeated call gets the same derived ID. No host route has been shown yet, and the shape predates this release. A fix is planned for v0.30.0.
- **A restart can store one half of a tool step without the other** ([#2191](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2191)): at a session's first turn after a restart, if the host gives a new identity to only the call or only the result of a tool step that is otherwise a replay, LCM-X stores that half and skips the other as a replay. The skipped half's text is already in the store from its earlier copy, so nothing is lost, but this occurrence's call and result are not stored together. It needs a host that changes the identity of one row of a pair and not the other. A fix is planned for a v0.30.x release after v0.30.0.
- **A crash right after a rotation can keep an extra reply in tests:** the reliability test that kills the agent right after a rotation can count one stored reply as extra. In every run checked for v0.29.1, the host had saved that reply too, so LCM-X matched the host and nothing was lost; the test's kill timing and its scorer are being fixed ([#861](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/861)). The older reports in [#824](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/824) have the same signature and are tracked in [#861](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/861).
- **Local embeddings on large, fully embedded stores (small hosts):** on a 2-CPU host with a 250,000-row fully embedded store, a semantic recall could use its full 8-second budget. Since v0.29.0, hosts with at most 2 effective CPUs answer from full text immediately when local embeddings are on by default (`degraded=true`, `cpu_limited`); explicit settings keep control. Faster exact semantic recall under contention is tracked in [#1586](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1586); the first attempt did not meet its memory bar, so no release is promised yet.
- **Local embeddings can outvote exact keyword hits:** with v0.29.0's deep-match fix, recall with embeddings off now returns its full 25 matches as well, and on the LoCoMo benchmark it answers more questions than the default local embeddings (1,165 vs 1,089 of 1,986 questions). Fusion gives the keyword arm half the weight of each embedding arm, so embedding-only hits can push an exact keyword hit out of the 25. Local embeddings still lead on LongMemEval-S (426 vs 408 of 500) and show no regression against v0.28.1. A fusion-weight change needs its own measurement and is planned for a minor release, not this patch ([#950](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/950)).
- **Python only: switching an existing config object to a cloud provider:** if code changes `embedding_provider` to a cloud provider on an `LCMConfig` that already resolved to the local default (with `dataclasses.replace` or attribute assignment), the enabled setting carries over, and that provider starts receiving text without `embeddings_enabled=True`. Settings from the environment and new `LCMConfig(...)` objects are not affected. Set `embeddings_enabled` explicitly when you switch providers in code. No fix is scheduled: [#1959](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1959) closed without a code change for this case.
- **Subagent work is not stored:** what a delegated subagent does in its own session, including its tool calls and intermediate results, is not stored by LCM-X. Only what the subagent returns to the parent conversation is stored, so `lcm_recall` cannot find a subagent's intermediate results. This isolation is not new in this release. Storing subagent sessions is planned for v0.30.0 ([#1931](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1931)).
- **A restart at an unlucky moment around compaction can store one summary row again** ([#1286](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1286)): three narrower restart timings stay open. They are a restart after a cleanup-only pass that the host kept without signalling that it committed it; with the non-default `compression.in_place=false`, a restart after the host published the new session but before LCM-X saw it start; and a restart while a second compaction still waits for the host to adopt it. Each can store the summary text once more as a message. Nothing is lost, and all three are older than v0.29.0.
- **A repeated message on a host that does not send its full history** ([#2124](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2124)): on a host that sends its full history at each turn, as the reference agent's host does, the lists below are replays after a restart, and storing nothing is correct. On a host that sends only new messages, or only its most recent ones, a message can be lost in two narrow cases, because the saved restart record can take a genuinely new message for a replay:
  - The record counts identical messages once, so a cleaned list that carries every distinct message since the last compaction, but fewer copies of a repeated one (a reply like "Done." given twice), counts as a replay of the conversation. A later batch of new messages that repeats every distinct message stored since that compaction can then be taken for a replay and not stored.
  - After a compaction, at a restart whose first list holds an older timestamped message and a new message without a timestamp, but not the rest of the session, LCM-X rewrites the record to that short list. After another restart, a new message identical to the untimestamped one, sent with the same older message, can be taken for a replay and not stored.

  Both cases come from the record v0.29.1 added; in them, v0.29.0 stores a second copy instead. Telling a replay from a genuine repeat on such hosts needs a record of which stored rows are duplicates, planned for a v0.30.x release after v0.30.0.
- **Hosts whose messages carry no timestamps:** LCM-X recognises a replay at a restart only from timestamped messages. On such a host, a message inserted earlier in the list, or a list of only new unstamped messages, can still be stored again at each restart, as on v0.29.0. Nothing is lost. The reference agent's host timestamps its messages, except the assistant and tool rows it rebuilds at a restart (see the restart item above).
- **Restart duplicates v0.29.1's restart fix does not cover yet:** in a few rarer orders of events the saved record is not rewritten, so the next restart can store messages a second time, as before that fix; none loses a message ([#2058](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2058), [#2119](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2119)). The same is true after a restart that follows a survival fit the host committed in place while compaction was on hold ([#2118](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2118)). When a host replaces an unstamped reply during a resend, or edits an unstamped assistant message in place, the new text is stored only at the next restart, along with a second copy of the conversation ([#2116](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2116), [#2058](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2058)). Two rarer passes that rewrite the host's list without changing which messages it holds, an overflow recovery and a compaction of only hidden rows, keep no saved record, as on v0.29.0, so a restart after one can store messages a second time ([#2134](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2134)).
- **Summary obligations after an out-of-order row in a session started by a compaction:** a later summary may not be required to cover some of the parent session's messages. The messages stay in the store and recall can still reach them. This predates v0.29.0; a fix is tracked for a v0.30.x release after v0.30.0 ([#2123](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2123)).
- **Cross-process cleanup:** another process sharing the store can still clear an empty live session binding and stall later compaction ([#753](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/753), [#761](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/761)).
- **Unloading the plugin without exiting leaves its store open** ([#2230](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2230)): on Hermes hosts that let a plugin be disabled or reloaded while the process keeps running, LCM-X does not close its engines when it is unloaded. Its database stays open, and its background work can keep running until the process exits; on Windows the database file stays locked until then. Stored rows are not affected. Restart the gateway after disabling the plugin.
- **Extra rows in one degraded mode:** when a child compaction can never publish (a different case from a single failed publication), three runtime hosts store extra rows and repeat user tags. No user content is missing. That reliability cell now gates on missing content only ([#1797](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1797), [#1900](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1900), [PR #1929](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/1929)).
- **Ignored and stateless sessions keep the doctor at a warning** ([#2234](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2234)): a session matched by `LCM_IGNORE_SESSION_PATTERNS` or `LCM_STATELESS_SESSION_PATTERNS`, such as a scheduled job, still writes an empty lifecycle row when it starts, so `lcm_doctor` reports the `lifecycle_fragmentation` warning after such runs. Nothing is stored for those sessions, and other stored rows are not affected, but the warning can hide a real fragmentation warning.
- **Hermes's empty-response retry rows are stored as conversation** ([#2087](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2087)): when the model returns an empty reply after tool calls, Hermes retries with an `(empty)` assistant row and a fixed re-prompt that its own session store does not keep. LCM-X stores both as ordinary rows, because they were part of the agent's context, so recall and summaries can include them. No user content is lost. No product change is planned; from v0.30.0 the release test kit counts these rows as host scaffolding.
- **Below the supported Hermes floor, a session can miss the rows after a saved tool result** ([#2539](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2539)): on Hermes 0.20.4 and earlier on Linux (the supported floor is 0.21.3), a session that holds a tool result Hermes saved to its temp folder and that ends while another session is active can miss the rows after that result. Fixed in v0.30.0 at default settings; with redaction on, see [#2604](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2604). Added after release, on 2026-11-12, from a reading of Hermes's source history rather than a run on an old Hermes.

## Qualification

As the first release train, v0.29.2 ran a smoke stage first at its release candidate, and no long row started until the smoke stage's checks passed (its mini rows M3, M1 and M2 ran alongside the long rows, as the release rules allow); then it ran the gauntlet rows its diff selects ([#1995](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1995), [PR #2088](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2088)). This diff changes the engine and the plugin's entry point, so it selected every memory row. Rows were selected and judged by the release spec as it stood on main at `b59c3b6`, because this release's own tree carries v0.29.1's spec; the release manager applied the row selector by hand, since the selector script has not merged. The "v0.29.2 only" rows cited below were added to that spec later, for this release. Where the release rules allow, rows reuse v0.29.1's baseline measurements from earlier runs; each receipt says so.

  The scorer fix, which judges this bar with v2 alone and removes its cap, is tracked in [#2214](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2214).

The first run ran out of its time budget on both versions alike (the row had budgeted about 11 minutes per question, and each took about 60), so it was ruled invalid, not a failure, and run once more with a larger time budget and more workers (6 instead of 4), with the same questions, trees and per-worker settings.
- D1 recall changes in the shipped local default, with embeddings off recorded beside it: **PASS**. Over all 500 LongMemEval-M questions, comparing each question's eight metrics per arm, `lcm_recall` and full-text search each had 0 flips against v0.29.1's recorded results (R@10 0.9005 on both versions); the A/A′ check had 0 discordant rows or rankings, and the health gate passed (500 = 470 scored + 30 abstention questions, 0 failed). How this row ran:
  - Its embedding cache was built in parallel parts under the call-index partition, whose proof passed on macOS and Linux at the instrument's commit ([PR #2099](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2099), [run 41815437846](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/actions/runs/41815437846)). Each role used two parts and was sealed only after its per-run checks passed, including a serial re-embedding check with 0 byte differences. A first launch with four parts per role ran out of memory within two minutes and was restarted with two. The proof has known gaps, none of which can turn a failing check into a pass: the receipt's thread-budget check leaves out a few seconds of worker warm-up, and the proof workflow's trigger misses two modules on the embedding path ([#1971](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/1971), folded from [#2200](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2200)).
  - Its batch-shape check failed by its own rule of zero ranking differences: over the same 10 questions, a cached and an uncached pass gave 2 questions different `lcm_recall` rankings, each a swap of adjacent results from the same set, while the six arms that read no clock matched exactly. `lcm_recall` weights each hit by its age, and a stored row's time is when it was ingested; the uncached pass ingests over hours while it embeds and the cached pass in minutes, so near-ties can swap. A blind adjudication attributed the failure to that clock, not to the cache, and the row ran on the cache under a release-manager decision bound to that exact receipt. Pinning the clock in this check is tracked in [#2270](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2270).
  - After the 63.7-hour run finished cleanly, its post-run health check stopped because the bench host's copy of the test kit lacked one folder of input files. The release manager finished the row without re-running it: the folder was copied in with every file's hash checked, the run's 298 output files were hashed before and after (unchanged), the runner's remaining steps ran, and the scoring ran on a hash-checked copy of the published outputs. The row ended on 2026-11-09, inside the release's 11-10 date ceiling.

This release's D4 runs both versions fresh. D8 runs its rule as written, with no waiver.
  - **D4.** LongMemEval-S (500 questions): 421 correct on this release against 427 on v0.29.1. 4 questions were right only on this release and 10 only on v0.29.1 (exact McNemar p = 0.18). LoCoMo (1,986): 1,083 against 1,088, with 33 and 38 (p = 0.64). D4 blocks only on a significant net loss (p < 0.05), and neither dataset has one. D4's own A/A′ placebo was accepted on every scored run. This release's, the one the rule reads, had 0 of 100 discordant on LongMemEval-S and 64 of 1,986 (3.2%) on LoCoMo (v0.29.1's: 1 of 100 and 67 of 1,986). The bar is at most 5% discordant with no significant A/A′ shift; LoCoMo's shift came close (exact McNemar p = 0.06).
  - **D8 on LoCoMo (446 adversarial questions): PASS.** This release is 0.7 points ahead of v0.29.1 (95% interval −1.5 to +2.6; the bar is a lower bound above −2). Its placebo, the same build run twice, stayed inside ±2 points (+0.2, interval −1.0 to +1.6), and no question was degraded on either version. v0.29.1's own LoCoMo placebo failed (−0.4, interval −3.0 to +1.4). The rule reads the release candidate's placebo.
  - **D8 on LongMemEval-S: not green (inconclusive).** Its placebo failed in both fresh pairs, on both versions, against a bar that asks each interval to lie inside ±2 points; in the 30-question category, one answer moves the difference 3.3 points. The rule re-runs a failed placebo once, in a fresh pair, and that pair failed too. The placebo's differences (rerun minus first run, in points, with 95% intervals), first pair then second:
    - this release: abstention (30 questions) −3.3 (−13.3 to +6.7) and +10.0 (−3.3 to +23.3); knowledge-update (78 questions) −1.3 (−3.8 to 0) and +1.3 (−2.6 to +6.4);
    - v0.29.1: abstention −3.3 (−10.0 to 0) and 0.0 (−10.0 to +10.0); knowledge-update −1.3 (−6.4 to +2.6) and −2.6 (−6.4 to 0).
    - Its comparison also misses the bound: abstention −10.0 points (interval −23.3 to +3.3) and knowledge-update −1.3 (−6.4 to +2.6).

    - Equal totals do not prove identical answers, so the release claims no D8 result here. The scorer printed a non-inferiority FAIL line for this dataset. With an invalid placebo, that line is not the verdict.
  - **How D4 was scored.** The row runner scores only when every version's run exits cleanly, and a failed D8 placebo exits with the same code as a failed D4 placebo, so this row would have ended unscored. The release manager first checked that every scored run's D4 placebo was accepted. Then they ran the runner's own final steps by hand, unchanged: the snapshot of each run, then the scorer for v0.29.1 and then for this release.
    - LongMemEval-S's first pair is not D4-scored. The scorer reads each dataset's latest run, a choice fixed before any result existed.
    - LoCoMo's second pair started only because v0.29.1's D8 placebo failed. It was stopped, and its partial runs were set aside, not deleted.

**Release-manager decisions.** 
- **Phase C doctor, caught host-trace and floor-host raw lossless bars:** not green, by the release spec's "v0.29.2 only" Phase C row ([PR #2213](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2213)). The row binds this release's first release candidate against v0.29.1, and no other row may cite it. The matched previous-GA disposition can't be used for a third release in a row. The test kit still counts these warnings and traces from log lines, not per host event, and it does not check the affected lifecycle rows against Phase B's identity rule ([#2212](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2212)).
- **D5-B doctor and LCM-X-frame traceback bars:** not green, by the spec's "v0.29.2 only" D5-B row ([PR #2213](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2213)). The reason is the same, plus two records the kit does not keep yet: a reorder count, and proof that the cells' config files differ only in paths.
- **Config-fixture warning on two Phase C hosts:** the spec's fixture-stamp row applies ([#432 comment 6282023562](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/432#issuecomment-6282023562), kit item 3); an independent check confirmed all six of its conditions.
- **Planted-fact probes:** 14 of 21 recalled exactly, against v0.29.1's 21 of 21, with 0 lost. The spec makes a drop below the previous GA a finding with a tracked issue, not a bar; [#944](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/944) recorded it, and the Phase C kit tracker [#432](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/432#issuecomment-6692750169) now tracks it.
- **#1501 fault cells:** two kill-timing cells were settled from repeats. Each shape also occurs on v0.29.1, and every release-candidate run is byte-identical to a v0.29.1 run.
- **D5 (reference-agent window):** not run, by a decision recorded before its window (see the D5 line above; [#2199](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2199)).
- **D2 and D3:** not green, by the release spec's v0.29.2-only D2/D3 row, adopted in [PR #2276](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/pull/2276).
  - This window's prospective A/A (v0.29.1 against itself, 54 replays) is inconclusive. In 20 replays the engine rejected a summary attempt; the D2 rule counts that as a failed attempt, and the budget allows 2 replacements. The release manager declined the one rerun the rule allows.
  - So this release has no paired comparison of facts kept against v0.29.1 on D2's material. Its compaction evidence is D7, D5-B and Phase C. D7 runs on the fleet's summary route with turn-end pacing, not D2's route and pacing, so it does not stand in for D2's comparison.
  - The same count finds rejected summaries in 25 of 55 and 27 of 55 replay attempts of v0.29.1's own A/A and D2. The D2 instrument counted those attempts as valid; read the way the rule is read now, both runs would have exceeded the replacement budget. v0.29.1's receipts stand as recorded; this note discloses it ([#2274](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2274)).
  - In 2 of the 54 replays, a slow rejected summary armed the 600 s compaction hold. While the hold lasts, the oldest live turns leave the model's context, including some that no summary covers. By reading the code (no D3 result exists for this A/A), they stay stored and can be retrieved, but lifting the hold does not return them to context ([#2272](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2272); the replay harness's side is [#2273](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2273)).
- **Host-cell raw lossless and zero-lost-rows bars:** not green on two cells because of the scorers' fragment caps, as on v0.29.1; integrity passes. A per-turn check without the scorers found every prompt and every delivered answer stored in all four cells. The fix, which judges this bar with multiset v2 alone and removes its cap, is tracked in [#2214](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2214). v0.29.1's notes said this scorer fix would go into v0.29.2. It did not: the kit change was not made before this release's runs, so the same limit showed again. The floor host's manual-setup turn 45, the doctor turn that closes the session, took about 388 s; host-cell timing is recorded, not judged.
- **#2330, an unreproduced loss lead:** disclosed under **Known issues**. GA does not wait for it: the session-end path and its readiness check are unchanged from v0.29.1, this release's reliability matrix showed no new failure against v0.29.1, and neither an engine-level attempt nor 8 repeats of the failing reliability cell with full logging reproduced it ([result](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2330#issuecomment-6705471802)). Any fix ships in a later release ([#2330](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2330)).
- **D1 batch-shape check:** its FAIL is attributed to `lcm_recall`'s clock, not to the cache, by a blind adjudication; D1 LOCAL ran on the cache under a decision bound to that receipt (see the D1 line above; [#2270](https://github.com/electricsheephq/lcm-x/issues/2270)).
- **D1 LOCAL's last steps:** finished without re-running the 63.7-hour run, after a missing kit input stopped its post-run health check (see the D1 line above).
- **D8 on LongMemEval-S:** not green: inconclusive after its one re-run, as the spec's D8 row says. By a release-manager decision recorded before any D4 accuracy comparison existed, the release ships with it rather than holding for more placebo runs. After the results, a second decision kept that course: the comparison misses its bound, but its gap to v0.29.1 (−10.0 and −1.3 points) is exactly what the release candidate's own rerun in the same pair recovered (+10.0 and +1.3); D4 on the same questions shows no significant loss; and no question was degraded (see the D4 line above). No bar changed, and every D8 number is published as measured in the attached receipts.
- **D4, scored by hand** with the row runner's own final steps, after checking every scored run's D4 placebo (see the D4 line above).
